title: Safe start after a restart
summary: A filling interrupted by a restart reopened the inlet valve by itself, because the fill request was retentive. After every start the inlet must stay closed until the operator presses Start again, while the batch count survives a warm restart.
objectives: Recognize a retentive actuator command as an unsafe start
Use FIRST_SCAN to bring a sequence into a safe initial state
Keep production data retentive while commands start safe
instructions: Build and load the program, set the PLC to RUN and press Start: the tank fills.
While it fills, make a warm restart in Advanced mode. Watch the inlet valve: with the starter program it opens again by itself.
Change the startup behavior so that after every start the inlet stays closed until Start is pressed, and keep Batches retentive.
Verify with a warm and a cold restart, check the diagnostic buffer for the start and first-scan events, then run Check.
hints: FIRST_SCAN is TRUE during exactly the first scan after each start.
Not every retentive value is safe to resume: a count may survive a restart, an actuator command usually must not.

scenarios.title: A filling interrupted by a warm restart, a full batch, then restarts

criteria.title: Start opens the inlet
criteria.onFail: InletValve did not open after Start.

criteria.title: The inlet stays closed after the restart
criteria.onFail: InletValve opened again right after the warm restart: the retained fill request resumed the filling.

criteria.title: The inlet waits for the operator
criteria.onFail: InletValve opened before Start was pressed again.

criteria.title: Start fills again after the restart
criteria.onFail: InletValve stayed closed after Start was pressed again.

criteria.title: The batch count survives a warm restart
criteria.onFail: Batches was not 1 after the warm restart: keep the batch count retentive.

criteria.title: A cold restart starts a new shift
criteria.onFail: After the cold restart Batches was not back to its initial value 0.
